Market stance

Cautious repair: Prof says the market has absorbed a lot and is closer to a bottom than a week ago, but iain warns damaged former leaders need weeks or months to rebuild their bases, so expect chop rather than a straight rebound.

Key watches

Catalysts

  • US–Iran headlines: Trump reportedly briefed on options including strikes (Enrich); “considering resuming the war with Iran as soon as tomorrow” (Prof)
  • Monday’s open after a split Friday — indexes drifted lower on quiet volume
  • ARKG $44 pullback watch and VRT zone (Friday’s close 194.32 inside it)

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
A quiet weekend tape: only four ticker ideas, no index calls, and no earnings chatter — the group’s camps are now bottom-watchers (Prof: closer to a bottom, be prepared to seize the opportunity) and chop-watchers (iain: damaged leaders take weeks or months to rebuild), with Enrich buying the other side of DiCarlo’s CIFR exit and DiCarlo himself adding zone watches instead of positions (VRT a zone buy, GLXY explicitly not taken). Sean and Venu posted process, not trades. Your process sides with the chop-watchers until price confirms: the only actionable levels are ARKG’s $44 pullback and VRT’s $147 stop, and the weekend’s Iran headlines are the reason Monday’s open — not Sunday’s opinions — gets the vote.

Sources & Methodology
  • Accounts scanned (7): Sean trades @SRxTrades · iain @ohiain · Enrich Trades @enrichtrades · Remz @Remzztrades · Prof @TheProfInvestor · Venu @Venu_7_ · Peter DiCarlo @pdicarlotrader. All seven accounts were readable this window (top ~5 posts visible per account before the login wall).
  • Posts window: Sat Oct 24 – Sun Oct 25, 2026 — everything visible after the Oct 24 feed’s window (which ended Oct 24, 11:45 UTC). Logged-out X shows only the ~5 most recent posts per account; posts truncated in the extraction itself (Sean’s system post, iain’s damaged-leaders post, Prof’s selloff post, Venu’s position-sizing post, DiCarlo’s VRT/GLXY posts) are quoted only to the visible cutoff.
  • Price data: Yahoo Finance daily data, as of the Fri Oct 23, 2026 close — markets were closed Sat–Sun, so this is the same close as the Oct 24 feed and no trend read changed from yesterday. Trader-stated = a level or call from their post, attributed by name. Chart check = computed by us from that data — it can confirm or push back on a trader’s framing, and it’s labeled every time.
  • Sector lines: each card’s sector/industry ETF comparison (Yahoo Finance, Fri Oct 23, 2026 close) — close, day change, Weinstein stage by the same 30-week MA method, and price vs the 50-week EMA. Mappings: AAPL→XLK, MSFT→IGV, NVDA→SMH, GOOGL/META→XLC, AMZN/TSLA→XLY, CIFR/GLXY→IBIT (spot bitcoin as the crypto/mining proxy — best-fit choice), ARKG→XBI (biotechnology — best fit for a genomics ETF), VRT→XLK (technology — best fit for data-center infrastructure).
  • Where none of the seven commented, the section says Unavailable / no trader signal — never “unchanged.” All four indexes are unavailable this window: no trader posted an index-specific level or call (the SPY panel carries Prof’s and iain’s general-market stances, but neither is an index call, so the strip label stays unavailable).
  • Qualifier rules (constructive pullback into a key MA/support, tightening base near highs, confirmed breakout; never extended/chased). Flagged watch: ARKG (pullback buy at Prof’s $44 into a multi-year base — the only genuine qualifier-style setup). Zone watch, not a confirmed setup: VRT (counter-trend zone buy with a defined $147 stop). Explicitly not qualifiers: CIFR (debated — the chart sides with DiCarlo’s prior-window exit over Enrich’s valuation call), GLXY (watch only — the trader himself is not taking it), GOOGL and TSLA (repair-only / declining), NVDA and AMZN (repair / between lines), AAPL (holds-only at the highs), MSFT (intact, trigger not fired), META (intact, barely).
  • Coverage note: yesterday’s ideas (ZS, NET, PANW, WM, TE) are not carried over — this window’s posts don’t repeat those calls, so they are not rows. No trader mentioned an earnings-only name this window, so there is no earnings-date catalyst list.
  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. Stage lives in the pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) and is kept out of the prose and the setup badges; traders’ own quoted words are exempt. No trend read changed from yesterday (same Friday close).
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels.
  • Trader charts: three embedded this edition — Prof’s ARKG monthly base chart, DiCarlo’s VRT weekly zone chart and DiCarlo’s GLXY weekly zone chart — retrieved from the photo links in their posts, verified as the correct tickers’ charts, and embedded below our charts in their panels with a link back to each post.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line’s endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built — all 45 checks (15 symbols × 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA) passed within 0.5%, most within 0.03%. The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only.
